newsitem.title: USA: Boeing expects about 340 deliveries in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Boeing expects about 340 deliveries in 1997.

text.p: Boeing Commercial Airplane Group, a division of Being Co., said Wednesday it expects to deliver about 340 airplanes of all models this year.
Boeing said it expects a production rate of 43 airplanes a month by the second quarter of 1988.
By the second quarter of 1998, production of the 737 will be 24 airplanes a month, Boeing said.
That number includes a combination of the Next-Generation and current model 737s, Boeing said.
In the second quarter of 1998, the 747 rate will increase from four airplanes a month to five, the company said.
The 777 rate will go from seven airplanes a month to five beginning in March 1998, the company said.
Production of the 757 will increase from four to five airplanes in the second quarter of 1998, Boeing said.
Production of the 767 is currently expected to remain at four airplanes a month throughout 1998, Boeing said.
